changes.before: Proposed annual data center load reporting to the Nebraska Power Review Board, public power service terms for large data centers, cost-shift protections, decommissioning resources, and community benefit agreements. An earlier record attributes removal of the annual PRB report from the LB1010 package to PRB minutes; the underlying minutes and amendment-level transfer have not been verified in this review.
changes.after: Introduced proposal: annual statewide data-center load reporting by the representative organization to the Power Review Board; service-cost/risk, decommissioning and community-benefit terms for a separately defined large data center (peak demand of at least 20 MW); and supplier-website disclosures. Direct comparison with enacted LB1010 shows a different data-center class starting at 10 MW, annual operator reports to the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment and Natural Resources Committee, and revised cost/decommissioning terms. The proposed section 70-1025 PRB-report amendment is absent from retained LB1010. This text comparison does not establish the AM2422 transfer path or validate the inherited PRB-minutes attribution.

changes.before: Adopted the Large Load Customer Regulation Act and changed cryptocurrency mining and data center provisions. Requires large-load interconnection standards, study fees, cost allocation to large-load customers, curtailment procedures, annual data center reports on electricity demand, water use, incentives, energy measures, renewable commitments, and service life, plus decommissioning-cost responsibility and community benefit agreements for data centers.
changes.after: Adopted the Large Load Customer Regulation Act for new or expanded retail-load interconnections exceeding 20 MW at one site, with interconnection standards, study fees, cost/risk allocation and curtailment procedures. A separate data-center definition in section 70-1506 uses peak demand of at least 10 MW. That section provides utility cost/load-study powers and requires annual owner/operator reports by September 30 to the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment and Natural Resources Committee, full decommissioning-cost responsibility and community benefit agreements with affected communities. The retained compiled statute identifies July 18, 2026 as section 70-1506’s effective date; that date is not generalized to every provision, and act-wide present force remains unverified.

scope: Reviewed source observations, classification correction and explicit unresolved facts; all IDs retained. No current-law census asserted.
